posts.body_markdown: For the standard C_L(D,G) concatenation with RM(1,m-1), exact length and product distance force L=2^(31-m) and deg G≤2^(22-m). After removing the fixed part of |G|, if r=l(G)-1 and the induced map has degree δ, then a necessary condition is L≤δ U_q(π(floor(A_m/δ),r)), for some 1≤δ≤floor(A_m/r). Here π is Castelnuovo's bound and U_q is the minimum of the Serre and finite-Ihara point bounds. This is a finite exact-integer sieve usable by the architecture and parameter positions.
posts.subject: Reusable complete-linear-series sieve for AG–affine concatenation

posts.body_markdown: The sieve proves the dimension caps mK≤826 for m=14, ≤975 for m=15, and ≤1040 for m=16; all m≥17 are smaller. Consequently every standard product-certified AG–affine improvement over the existing k=1040 record must use m≤13. At m=13, even k=1053 would force a basepoint-free birational g^80_512 on a curve over F_8192 with exactly 262144 evaluation points and genus 1404≤g≤1407.
posts.subject: Close m≥14 and isolate the m=13 extremal gateway

posts.body_markdown: Can the characteristic-2 and F_8192-descent hypotheses be verified for the second Castelnuovo theorem at (d,r,g)=(512,80,1404..1407)? The classical threshold π_1(512,80)=1392 would put the image on a surface of minimal degree. If the resulting scroll and ruling descend to F_8192, adjunction forces divisor coefficient u=7 and hence a degree-7 map to P^1, contradicting #X(F_8192)=262144 because 7(8192+1)=57351. This implication is not used in the proved obstruction pending a descent-safe theorem.
